lines.english: "…Are you certain that you got such a call, and that it came from one of our guests?"
"That's why I'm in such a hurry! Every second matters here!"
"However… I still haven't confirmed that you truly have any relation to our guest…"
"Didn't I already tell you to confirm it with her agent? Did you get through to them?"
"No, I couldn't possibly… After all, it's 2 AM."
"I'm telling you I have no time to lose! Didn't I explain to you earlier exactly the kind of things she said over the phone?"
"It would be very grave if it was true… though I'd note that just the other day, we had a journalist pretending to be a friend of hers and made it all the way to her room."
"Fine, then! I'll do it on my own. You can go ahead and call the police. If it turns out I'm lying, you can just have me removed on the spot."
"…Alright then! However, I'll be the first to try to reach out to her. Is that okay?"
"Go ahead. Please, save Kazusa…"
"…Miss Touma? I'm sorry for bothering you at this hour."
It seems that from my insistence, the gravity of the situation has finally come through to the room clerk. After nervously clearing his throat, he begins to knock on the door.
"Miss Touma, Miss Touma… I apologize for the intrusion, but if you are awake, could you please open the door?"
However, neither his knocks nor his calls are loud enough to go through the bulky door and reach the other side of the spacious suite.
"…It seems she is not awake."
"I keep telling you she isn't responding! We couldn't get through to her even when you called her on the phone by the front desk!"
"Well, that would be…"
"Kazusa! Kazusa! I'm begging you, please answer!"
"H-Hey, stop that! You're disturbing the other guests."
"This is not the time to worry about that! If she's hurt, it'll be on your conscience!"
From the very start, the hotel staff have been on alert ever since I rushed in to the front desk.
When I told them I was acquainted with Touma Kazusa and that I needed to enter her room right away, their suspicion only grew further.
"Kazusa! Are you okay!? I know you're in there. Talk to me!"
"A-Are you certain…"
"If it turns out that something awful has happened and you didn't help, I'll never forgive you…! I'll put a curse on those very rules of yours."
"…! Miss Touma, Miss Touma! Are you okay!?"
I spent dozens of minutes having a fruitless exchange with the front desk employee, who told me that the rules meant that giving her a phone call on my behalf was the best they could do.
When I told them that I hadn't heard from her since she sent her farewell on my answering machine, they finally became more cooperative.
However, their doubts were still very strong.
"Damn it… damn it! What am I supposed to do… What the hell am I supposed to do?"
"How strange… No response even with all this noise we're making."
"That's what I've been trying to explain to you all this time!"
They followed me all the way to Kazusa's room, but still insistent on following the rules, they refused to do more than wait for Kazusa to open the door.
Still, this is only natural…
They value their guests above all else, and have no reason to trust a dubious stranger who showed up in the middle of the night.
"Damn it… better call the police. No, an ambulance! Excuse me, go to the front desk and call…"
"…Let's try to open the door first. At this point, we have no other choice."
Up until now, he had been adamant about following the rules to the letter, but now it seems my desperation had finally reached him.
"However, I will enter first. I can't have anyone but staff entering someone's room without permission."
"Oh, alright…"
"If you can't promise me that, then I'll have no choice but to see you out."
They were afflicted with the same feeling of uncertainty, yet I could sense their doubt in me disappearing, if only a little bit.
"I'll leave it to you… Please help her!"
Perhaps my desperate pleas had finally reached the human side of the employees.
"Now then, Miss Touma. I am really sorry about this. But due to this being an emergency, I'll be entering your room."
He then grabs a key out of his pocket, and begins to move it toward the keyhole.
But at the very moment the key is about to enter, the keyhole moves backward as if avoiding it.
Or rather, more accurately…
"My condolences…"
The door opened.
"He put on a really convincing act, didn't he? But he's just another journalist… and a big, fat liar."
"Kazusa…"
And out of that door came a figure I hadn't seen for a whole day…
"He's acting all surprised. But that's all part of his act. He's been using you from the start."
"Ee…eeeh!?"
"I was so worried about you… I'm so glad, Kazusa…"
It's just that…
Her "farewell" wasn't as profound in meaning as I had thought.
"It's so cold…"
It had already stopped snowing.
Instead of piling up, the snow melted onto the road. The wind, too, is unreasonably cold.
The sky is starting to clear up. By daybreak, I'm sure we'll be able to see the bright sun again.
"Why did you come here?"
As I breathe into my hands for warmth, I see a white puff that soon disappears into the darkness of the night.
"Making such a scene at this time of night… You'd have no right to complain if the police came and took you away."
After that ordeal, rather than pressing me for answers, the employee just turned bright red in bewilderment at the sight of Kazusa.
"I wanted to see you right away…"
In the end, Kazusa brought the whole fiasco to a close with the single, dull statement of, "this guy is with me."
"…It's been a whole day since I left. How is this right away?"
The room clerk chalked it up to it just being a lovers' quarrel. He's probably heaving a sigh at the front desk as we speak.
"You're right… sorry for taking so long."
"Idiot…! No one was waiting for you…"
…The problem is, he wouldn't exactly be wrong in that assumption.
"Where are you going?"
"Nowhere in particular…"
Amidst the cool night wind, I walk around town with Kazusa at my heels.
"What are you thinking? Bringing someone out in this cold."
Her mood must be soured by being called outside in the middle of the night.
And overwhelmed from all the things that had happened.
"Want to stop by at a family restaurant, then? We can talk there."
"It's not like we… have nothing to talk about."
"I see…"
"…So walk a bit slower, would you? Try to imagine what it's like having to catch up with you."
"…Sorry."
In spite of that, Kazusa continues to follow me.
She's desperately trying to match my pace so she won't get left behind.
"But it's still cold… very cold."
"Come here. I should be able to protect you from the wind, at least."
"Okay…"
At last, she lines up perfectly next to me.
"It was snowing up until a while ago…"
"I know… I watched it from the hotel window."
"So you were awake."
"…So what if I was?"
Because she has no one else but me right now.
Because no matter how much she curses at me and no matter how much she tries to push me away, deep down, she wants me by her side.
I wonder if things would have been that much easier for the both of us if that self-aggrandizing conclusion was merely something I'd conjured up…?
"How long have you known? About mom, I mean."
"Not very long… for about a week."
"Why would my mom tell you, when she kept it a secret even from me? Why?"
"That's because…"
"She trusts you more than she trusts me, is that it? Because you're more reliable than me…?"
"I practically forced it out of her. Just like how I forced you out here tonight."
"Then why didn't you tell me… Why did you keep it a secret from me!?"
"Because I knew you would react like this…"
Sure enough, she goes quiet, and all but outright admits that I'm right by hanging her head.
That without Youko-san to cling to, she no longer has any idea how to move forward.
Only stretching her hand out to the empty air in the vain hope of someone grabbing it. Walking all alone, crying, and lost.
"So that's why… that's why you've been so nice to me recently. That's why it all felt so forced."
"Did you hate it?"
"Of course I didn't hate it… How could I ever hate you treating me nicely?"
"I wonder about that…"
…Only stretching her hand out to seek me out.
"But I wanted you to act more natural. I never wanted to find out that you had an ulterior motive."
"Acting the way you want me to is easier said than done…"
I could no longer immerse myself in these convenient delusions.
"Kazusa has been in love with me for the past five years."
That dream-like reality. That one unbelievable delusion that could never come true.
And yet she herself reaffirmed those emotions with such unbelievable fervor.
"You thought I was insufferable, didn't you? But you had to stay with me because of what happened with mom."
"I've already told you, that's not the case…"
"Because if I knew the truth, you thought I might try to kill myself. That's what you thought, wasn't it?"
"No, it wasn't. I know that you're not that inconsiderate of others."
"Ah…"
"…But I don't think you can recover on your own two feet, either. You just don't have the courage. And you're not strong enough, either."
"W-What's that supposed to mean…?"
The person in front of me truly is as lost as I imagined she was.
She's too afraid to go forward, but also too afraid to give up. So she ends up stuck in place…
"…Looks like you've got it all figured out. Do you take yourself for my guardian?"
"…Yes, I do. Because I want to protect you."
"I… I don't need that sense of obligation from you! Not even I would stoop so low as to accept being protected by a man who doesn't even love me."
"Get it together, then! Show Youko-san and me that you can manage to live on your own!"
"You can't, can you? You could never manage to do that, could you!?"
"That's… not true… After all, I've always been alone… Up until five years ago, I've been living all by myself…"
"You weren't alone at all. You only convinced yourself that you were."
"You were living on Youko-san's money, and not least of all her kindness. You were living life as you saw fit, and all the while you hated her for it."
"What… What are you trying to say!?"
If no one reaches out a hand to her now, then she's going to rot away without taking another step forward.
Even if nothing happens to cause her harm, it wouldn't surprise me if she still ended up that way. That's how weak she is.
"You've always been like this. You're selfish, you're a slob, and a failure of a human being. …Just having to look at you is getting me irritated."
"Haruki…?"
"And you're a bad person too. Your personality, your attitude, and your inability to see anything through. The only things you have going for you are your looks and your piano!"
"But… Haruki…"
That's why when I push her away even a little bit, her voice starts shaking in an instant.
"You look beautiful, but you're rotten on the inside. Even if people accept you as a genius musician, you'll never be accepted as a proper member of society."
"Stop it… Stop it!"
Unable to maintain her facade of vanity, she becomes unable to hold back her shock and tears.
"On top of being awful, you've made it even worse by falling in love with me. Do you have any idea how much pain you have caused me because of that?"
"You don't have to be so mean… It's not like I don't already know that."
Moreover, she's looking at me with desperate, upturned eyes full of tears, as if she were an abandoned pup clinging to me.
"That's why people like you struggle so much! On top of being talented, you stubbornly refuse to fit in with the rest of society. You're left with almost no social skills whatsoever…"
"I already know that… Why are you telling me this now…!?"
She really is so weak.
"Kazusa… you really are useless."
"Shut up…"
The image I had in my head of the cool, dignified lone wolf that I used to have a crush on crumbles away.
"You can't live on your own, yet you're so picky about those who try to help you that you ruin things for yourself."
"I said stop already! Just shut up… please, just shut up!"
She's a rabbit in wolf's clothing… Acting like she prefers solitude yet dies if left alone. The kind of odd species that would inevitably go extinct.
"How were you planning to live on without Youko-san and me!?"
"I don't know! I've never thought about something so ridiculous!"
"It's because you are so helpless, because you are so unbelievably weak that…"
"Haruki! I told you…!"
"That… I have to do something, right?"
…I just can't bring myself to abandon someone as hopeless as she is.
If Youko-san can't do it, then I will. I'll have to be the one to reach out to her.
"You know… I, as awful as you are, I love you. More than anyone else in the world."
"…Eh… Eeh!?"
"I can't bear seeing you unhappy!"
"…Haruki?"
No… I want to be the one to reach out to her.
"If I am what you need to be happy… No, if I am what you need to continue living…"
"Then I'll be there for you. …Even if it means I have to throw everything else away."
